description: Refactor the existing Model Creation Flow to keep the current four-step user experience while separating model training, evaluation, fine-tuning, and final model persistence. Training and fine-tuning must not commit the model to the database. The model is persisted only when the user explicitly clicks Save Model in Step 4.
progress_note: MODEL-FLOW-000, -001, -002 completed 2026-08-18 (3 of 10 features — denominator moved 9->10 on 2026-08-19 when MODEL-FLOW-009 was added; see that feature's own status for why it's separate from the -003 catalogue work, not an increment to it). Still blocked overall: MODEL-FLOW-005 remains blocked pending a definition of 'fine-tuning' (decisions.fine_tuning_undefined); MODEL-FLOW-009 (lstm/gru) is newly blocked pending a windowing pipeline. -003 is in_progress (T10's catalogue half resolved 2026-08-19, AutoML half still blocked) — the rest of this note (-004/-006/-007/-008 status) pre-dates 2026-08-19 and was not re-audited this pass.

draft_persistence.chosen: B — ModelDraft as a database entity
draft_persistence.rationale: A training container has no browser: it authenticates with a run token hashed into a row, reads its spec from /claim, and writes logs and metrics back over HTTP. A client-only jotai draft (MODEL-FLOW-002 as built) is unreachable from that process, so training could not run against it at all. Mirrors DatasetDraft (DS-LAKE-005), which solved the identical problem for the dataset wizard and is already proven in production — including the abandon-not-delete rule and the adopt-by-pointer save.

rejected.A — nullable modelId on ModelTrainingRun: Would work, but leaves the draft's own configuration (name, location, dataset, algorithm, target, split) with nowhere server-side to live, so Step 4's Save Model would still have to trust a client-supplied config. DatasetDraft exists precisely to avoid that.
rejected.C — create Model at training, flip statu: Directly contradicts the global definition of done. Also leaks: an abandoned wizard leaves a Model row in the workspace listing.

persistence_boundary_clarified.note: 'No database commit before Save Model' means no persistent MODEL record. It does not mean no writes at all. ModelDraft, ModelTrainingRun, ModelTrainingRunLog and ModelFineTuningJob are all written before Save Model — they are job and workspace rows, the same class of row PreprocessingJob and DatasetArtifact occupy during the dataset wizard, where DS-LAKE-005 already accepted them. What Save Model creates is the Model itself, and it adopts everything else by pointer.

artifact_scope.note: Run outputs are written under drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/, not models/{modelId}/runs/{runId}/ — a modelId does not exist when the container uploads. Save Model adopts those objects by pointer (never copies bytes), the same rule DatasetArtifact.datasetId's own schema comment states. is_model_run_key/model_run_key must accept the draft scope; see MODEL-FLOW-006-T07.

fine_tuning_undefined.note: MODEL-FLOW-005 is BLOCKED on a definition, not on engineering. train.py fits once and exits; HistGradientBoostingRegressor has no incremental warm start. 'Fine-tuning' here most likely means 'retrain with a different hyperparameter set, reusing the same split', which is a search loop, not fine-tuning in the transfer-learning sense. Naming it correctly changes what T01-T08 are.

features.title: Unblock the Training Path — Correctness Prerequisites
features.description: Four defects that make the existing training path either impossible to start or unsafe to trust. None is a refactor; every one is a correctness fix that MODEL-FLOW-003 onward depend on. T02 in particular gates every metric Step 3 displays.
features.reaudit_note: Re-audited 2026-08-18 before implementation, by reading each named file directly (not by report). Five of the seven original tasks (T01, T03, T04, T05, T07) described code that was ALREADY CORRECT at commit 1df3c53 — the audit that produced this feature had drifted from the tree. T03's premise was inverted (memory 8 GiB > tmpfs 2 GiB, already consistent, not the reverse). Only T02 and T06 were live defects; both are now fixed. The likely cause of the drift: images/trainer/train.py:180-203 held a half-applied T02 patch (a broken orphan build_feature_spec with an undefined _reads_tag and an unimportable `spec = {...}` set-of-Ellipsis) — evidence someone started T02 before, landed the Pydantic field and helper functions, and left the wiring. See T08-T10 for defects found during re-audit that were NOT in the original task list.

tasks.title: Fix unsatisfiable artifact precondition in createRunService
tasks.detail: createRunService requires artifact.type === 'GOLD' AND artifact.datasetId != null. saveDraftAsDatasetService sets datasetId on the FINAL row only — a GOLD artifact keeps just its draftId — so no run can ever be created. Change to type === 'FINAL'. Nothing is lost: promoteDraftArtifactToFinalService copies objectKey/checksum/featureSpecKey from its source verbatim and writes no bytes, so FINAL and its GOLD parent are the same object with the same feature spec, and FINAL additionally carries the validationKey proving it passed the gate. Also restore the findUnique call, which was overwritten with a fragment of saveDraftAsDatasetService (references tx/finalArtifact/dataset, none in scope — the file does not compile).
tasks.verification_note: Re-verified 2026-08-18 by reading model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts directly: line 65 already reads `artifact.type !== 'FINAL'` (not 'GOLD'), the findUnique at line 61 is intact, and `tsc --noEmit` reports zero errors in this module. Already satisfied — no code change needed.

tasks.title: Record the target in feature_spec.json so the leakage guard can fire
tasks.detail: train.py::assert_no_target_leakage reads derived_from_target, target_y and target_scaled from feature_spec.json. build_feature_spec(features, selected_columns, scalers) has no target parameter and emits none of the three, so `derived` is always empty and the guard returns before checking anything. This is the highest-severity item in the plan: the failure it catches LOOKS LIKE SUCCESS. A lab target sampled daily against a 1-minute PI grid with any target-derived lag feature yields R² near 1.0, and Step 3 would render that with a convincing actual-vs-predicted chart. Requires threading the target through FeaturesRequest -> the NestJS DTO -> the client's Step 4 call, and computing derived_from_target from the feature configs. target_y/target_scaled/derived_from_target must NOT enter featureHash: they describe how a run READS the artifact, not how it was built, so two runs with different targets against the same bytes must still share a hash.
tasks.verification_note: Implemented 2026-08-18. build_feature_spec gained an optional 4th target_y param; when set it adds target_y/target_scaled/derived_from_target AFTER the hash is computed (never entering it). derived_from_target is a TRANSITIVE closure (a forward pass tracking every column that reads the target or an already-tainted column), not a direct-read check — the original task text under-specified this, and a direct-read predicate would miss a feature chained off an earlier target-derived feature. artifact_service.py::features() now also calls the existing (previously orphaned) force_keep_target helper once and reuses that same effective column list for both select_columns and build_feature_spec, so the spec never claims a different column set than what was actually written. Threaded through CreateFeaturesSchema (NestJS), both python call sites (inline /features route and the async job path incl. readFeatureRecipe), and the client (dwTargetTagAtom -> useDatasetGoldWarm -> startFeaturesJob), with targetTag added to the warming effect's dependency list. assert_target_is_unscaled was deliberately left uncalled — a scaled target is recorded truthfully and blocked later at training time by train.py's existing check, not at dataset-save time. Verified via 6 new pytest cases in test_feature_spec_quirks.py (14/14 pass) proving build_feature_spec's own contract, PLUS a 7th seam test (test_features_force_keeps_target_through_select_columns in test_artifact_service_features.py) proving the wiring at the call site actually works: with selected_columns deliberately omitting the target, both the WRITTEN BYTES and the spec's selectedColumns retain it — the first-pass draft of this note cited only the unit-level tests, which would have missed a broken call site. Full apps/python suite: 617 passed, 1 pre-existing unrelated failure (test_features_writes_feature_spec_sidecar_and_returns_its_key, confirmed via git stash to predate this branch), 66 skipped.

tasks.title: Fix container resource limits (tmpfs exceeds the memory cap)
tasks.detail: CORRECTED 2026-08-18: this task's premise was inverted against the tree. trainning-container.authorized.service.ts:27-29 sets Memory to 8 GiB (`8 * 1024 ** 3`) and line 92 sets the /scratch tmpfs to 2 GiB (`size=2g`) — memory already exceeds the tmpfs, which is the consistent direction, not the reverse this task described. Neither value is overridden by any TRAINING_MEMORY_BYTES/TRAINING_NANO_CPUS env var in .env or .env.example, so these code defaults are the effective, already-safe limits.
tasks.verification_note: Verified 2026-08-18 by reading trainning-container.authorized.service.ts:19-30,83-95 directly. Already satisfied — no code change needed. The residual risk the original reasoning still correctly names (tmpfs pages are charged to the container's memory cgroup, so /scratch + the in-memory DataFrame + sklearn all share the 8 GiB cap) remains true and worth monitoring under a large artifact, but is not a defect to fix.

tasks.title: Align the container's callback base path with the controller
tasks.detail: train.py builds API = {API_BASE}/internal/model/runs/{RUN_ID}; ModelRunAuthorizedController is @Controller('authorized/model/runs') behind the /api/v1 global prefix. Every callback 404s, starting with /claim. Pick one: either the container's path gains the real prefix, or the controller moves to internal/model/runs — the latter reads better, since 'authorized' means a user JWT everywhere else in this codebase and this controller explicitly does not take one.
tasks.verification_note: Verified 2026-08-18 by reading images/trainer/train.py:29-42 directly. Line 40 already builds `{API_BASE}/api/v1/authorized/model/runs/{RUN_ID}`, matching the controller's `authorized/model/runs` path behind `setGlobalPrefix('api')` + URI versioning v1. Already satisfied — no code change needed. Note: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile, so a deployed image tagged scgc/soft-sensor-trainer:1.0.0 could still carry stale train.py — the repo source is correct, deployment currency was not verified.

tasks.title: Stop leaking tokenHash from cancelRunService
tasks.detail: Its findFirst has no omit, and the early return for an already-terminal run returns that row straight to the caller. The other three read paths already omit it. A token hash reaching the browser is not exploitable on its own, but it is the kind of leak that becomes one after any change to how tokens are compared.
tasks.verification_note: Verified 2026-08-18 by reading model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:158-186 directly. `omit: { tokenHash: true }` is present on both the findFirst (line 167) and the update (line 177); the early-terminal-run return at line 170 returns the already-omitted row. Already satisfied — no code change needed.

tasks.title: Remove the debug print of the presign request
tasks.detail: routers/preprocess.py::presign_artifact prints the whole request body. Neither the request nor the response should reach a log: a presigned URL is a bearer capability for the artifact bytes, and anyone who can read the log can download them for the lifetime of the URL.
tasks.verification_note: Fixed 2026-08-18: deleted the `print(f"Presign request for artifact {body}")` at routers/preprocess.py:488-489. Confirmed this router module has no other importer besides main.py's route mount.

tasks.title: Delete the dead tag_stats path
tasks.detail: artifact_service.tag_stats duplicates column_stats line for line, references TagStatsRequest which is not imported (the module fails to import), and has no router endpoint. Its NestJS counterparts are equally broken: getDraftArtifactTagStatsService uses an unimported PythonTagStatsSchema, and getDraftArtifactStatsController calls a method name that does not exist. Remove all four, plus the POST /:id/artifacts/:artifactId/stats route.
tasks.verification_note: Verified 2026-08-18 via repo-wide grep for tag_stats|TagStatsRequest|PythonTagStatsSchema|getDraftArtifactTagStats|getDraftArtifactStatsController — zero hits anywhere in apps/backend, apps/python, or packages. Already satisfied — no code change needed.

tasks.title: Delete the orphan half-applied build_feature_spec in train.py
tasks.detail: Found during T02 re-audit, not in the original task list. images/trainer/train.py:180-203 held a second, broken copy of build_feature_spec: `spec = {...}` is a set containing Ellipsis (the next line's item assignment would raise TypeError), `_reads_tag` is undefined anywhere in the repo, and `feature_column_name` is not imported into train.py. Unreachable from main() — the trainer only ever reads feature_spec.json, it does not author one; the connector (feature_spec_service.py) owns that. Latent, not fatal, but the most plausible explanation for how T02 came to look already-attempted.
tasks.verification_note: Fixed 2026-08-18: deleted the orphan function. Confirmed via grep that nothing imports train.py as a module (it is a standalone container ENTRYPOINT).

tasks.title: Harden is_model_run_key against path traversal
tasks.detail: Found during re-audit. object_store.py's is_model_run_key was a substring test (`key.startswith('models/') and '/runs/' in key'`), so a malformed model_id like '../../x' would pass. Currently unreachable — the sole caller (presign_model_run_upload) builds keys only from run.modelId/run.id off the ModelTrainingRun row, never from a container-supplied id directly — but MODEL-FLOW-003-T08 widens this predicate to accept the draft scope too, which is when a malformed id becomes reachable.
tasks.verification_note: Fixed 2026-08-18: rewrote as a structural check requiring exactly 4 non-empty path segments after MODEL_ROOT (model_id/runs/run_id/filename), none of them '.' or '..', mirroring is_committed_artifact_key's sibling shape. Confirmed the sole caller (artifact_service.presign_model_run_upload) still passes with well-formed keys. Added test_is_model_run_key_rejects_traversal_and_malformed_segments to tests/test_object_store.py (8 cases: valid key, '../../x' traversal, mid-path '..', double-slash, extra segment, wrong literal, empty segment, wrong root) — all pass. This is the actual claim the task makes; a passing pre-existing suite alone would not have proven it.

tasks.title: Collapse the degenerate ternary in watch()
tasks.detail: Found during re-audit. trainning-container.authorized.service.ts:133 was `status: StatusCode === 0 ? 'FAILED' : 'FAILED'` — both branches identical, so the condition is dead code. The failureReason string two lines below correctly distinguishes a clean exit that never called /complete from a genuine crash; only the status assignment was affected.

features.title: Model Draft Workspace as a Database Entity
features.implementation: SUPERSEDED-then-REWORKED. The first pass built a client-only jotai draft (apps/client/store/model-pipeline.ts: DraftState + mpDraftIdAtom/mpDraftStateAtom/mpTrainingResultAtom/mpEvaluationResultAtom/mpArtifactRefAtom, wired into resetWizardAtom). That state is still useful as wizard UI state and was NOT deleted — but it could not serve as the draft MODEL-FLOW-003 needs: a training container has no browser and reads its spec from an HTTP endpoint backed by a row. See decisions.draft_persistence. T06-T09 (2026-08-18) added the server-side ModelDraft beneath it: Prisma entity + migration, ModelTrainingRun repointed with a CHECK constraint, a new authorized/model-draft module (create/get/patch/abandon), and a client sync hook (mpServerDraftIdAtom + useModelDraftSync) wired into Phase2TrainingConfig.

features.title: Training Against a Draft, With No Model Commit
features.implementation: Backend done 2026-08-18 (T02/T04/T07/T08) — see each task's verification_note. Client done same day (T01/T03/T04/T05/T06/T09): use-model-training.ts rewritten — no longer calls useModelCommit(); instead validates (single target, single algorithm, algorithm in the training container's supported set, AutoML toggles off, dataset has a FINAL artifact), calls the new modelDraftRunService.create via authorized/model-drafts/:draftId/runs, and polls modelDraftRunService.get on a 2.5s interval until the run reaches a terminal status, resuming the poll on remount from ModelDraft.currentRunId if a run is still in flight. useModelDraftSync now exposes ensureDraftId so Start Training can guarantee a draft exists even if the 600ms PATCH debounce hasn't fired yet. TrainState gained lastLog (shown as text in place of the old fake progress bar — T09); mpTrainingResultAtom/mpArtifactRefAtom are populated from the completed run's metrics/modelKey on SUCCEEDED (T05/T06). T10 is the one open item, and its catalogue half was resolved 2026-08-19: validation now enforces exactly one target and one algorithm before a run is created; the wizard's algorithm catalogue (now 12 entries: ols/ridge/hist_gradient_boosting/svm/mlp/grp/pls/random_forest/lightgbm/xgboost/lstm/gru) is intentional per product decision, and train.py's build_model was extended to implement 10 of the 12 (images/trainer/train.py) — lstm/gru remain deferred to MODEL-FLOW-009 and disabled inline in the wizard. features.title: Sequence Model Training (LSTM/GRU) — Deferred, Needs a Windowing Pipeline
features.blocked_on: lstm/gru need a data-SHAPE change (2D samples x features -> 3D samples x timesteps x features) upstream of the split, plus a sequence_length hyperparameter and a deep-learning runtime this image doesn't carry. This is not a build_model branch — recorded separately per CLAUDE.md 17 (missing infrastructure, unclear contract) rather than left as an omission when MODEL-FLOW-003-T10's catalogue half was resolved (images/trainer/train.py; apps/client/store/model-pipeline.ts Algorithm catalogue).
features.description: The wizard's Algorithm catalogue includes lstm and gru; train.py's build_model raises a named error for both rather than the generic 'Unsupported algorithm' message, and the wizard disables both inline (AlgorithmSelector) so a user cannot select a run that will always fail. This feature is what it would take to actually run them — not scoped or estimated as part of the 10-algorithm tabular extension, because the shape of the work is different in kind, not degree.

tasks.title: Design the windowing step (2D -> 3D) and where it runs in the pipeline
tasks.detail: Sequence models need (samples, timesteps, features); train.py currently builds a flat (samples, features) frame and hands feature_cols straight to fit(). Windowing must happen BEFORE chronological_split (train.py:143-164) — windowing after the split lets a window's timesteps span the train/test boundary, which is exactly the ordering bug the module docstring already warns about for the non-Good-target drop (train.py:8-12), just one step later in the pipeline.

tasks.title: Extend the leakage guard to cover window-straddling, not just row-wise lags
tasks.detail: assert_no_target_leakage (train.py:101-140) reasons about row-wise lag features via the target's labelled-vs-row median sampling gap — it says nothing about a WINDOW that starts before the cut and ends after it. A window straddling chronological_split's boundary is a leakage path today's guard cannot see, because it was written for a different failure shape (a lag column repeating the current target value, not a window spanning two sides of a split). This needs its own check, not a parameter on the existing one.

tasks.title: Add sequence_length (and validate epochs/batch_size/hidden_size against it) to the hyperparameter contract
tasks.detail: Correction to an earlier framing of this gap: HYPERPARAMS.lstm / HYPERPARAMS.gru (apps/client/lib/training-config.ts:212-264) already collect epochs, batch_size, and hidden_size — those are NOT missing. The one genuinely missing field is sequence_length, the value that actually defines the window this feature needs. Both the DTO's HyperparametersSchema and the client catalogue need it added, and epochs/batch_size need a documented default now that they will actually be consumed by a real fit loop instead of sitting unused.

tasks.title: Add a deep-learning runtime to the trainer image and re-audit sizing
tasks.detail: Needs tensorflow or torch (+~1.5-2 GB), which changes build time and the memory/tmpfs sizing MODEL-FLOW-000-T03 already audited and closed (8 GiB Memory, no swap; 2 GiB tmpfs /scratch sharing the same cgroup — trainning-container.authorized.service.ts). That audit's 'not a defect to fix' conclusion was reached against the current sklearn-only image; it does not automatically extend to an image carrying a full DL framework and this needs its own pass, not an inherited one.

acceptance_criteria: A windowing step exists and runs strictly before chronological_split, never after.
A window cannot straddle the train/test cut — verified by a leakage-style guard, not by convention.
sequence_length is a real, validated hyperparameter end to end (client catalogue, DTO, train.py), not inferred or hardcoded.
The trainer image's memory/tmpfs sizing is re-verified against the DL runtime it now carries, not assumed unchanged from the sklearn-only audit.

Until all of the above land, lstm/gru remain refused — at the API (TrainingAlgorithmEnum), in the wizard (AlgorithmSelector, disabled with a reason), and in build_model (named backstop error) — never silently mapped to a tabular algorithm.

features.title: New Step 2 — Dataset Review before Training Configuration
features.description: A review step between Model Setup and Training Configuration. Shows which data source the selected dataset came from, its per-tag statistics, the same DataAnalysisCard the dataset wizard's Step 3.1 uses, and the held-out validation window — so an engineer sees WHAT they are about to train on before configuring HOW. Includes a route back into the dataset wizard for a dataset that needs changing.
userDecisions: STEP COUNT (resolved): five steps. The flow becomes Setup -> Dataset Review -> Training Configuration -> Evaluation -> Save Model. This file's global_definition_of_done currently asserts four steps in four separate lines and MODEL-FLOW-008 verifies by step number; all of them are rewritten as part of T01 rather than left to contradict the feature that renumbered them.

EDIT DATASET RE-ENTRY (resolved): warn-and-navigate, NOT an overlay and NOT a full URL-addressable resume. An overlay would keep the model wizard mounted and make Back a close rather than a rehydration — genuinely smaller than a resume mechanism — but it rests on three unverified assumptions about the dataset wizard (mountable outside its route, no atom collision, no reset-on-mount). Three unknowns for one button is a poor trade against an honest dialog. The draft is PATCHed current before navigating and is resumable from the models list (T08).
findings: EVERY READ THIS STEP NEEDS ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY PROVEN. DS-LAKE-013 wired the dataset library to its committed artifact: useArtifactMetadata, useArtifactColumnStats, useArtifactRows and useArtifactCorrelation all take (datasetId, artifactId) and return bounded server responses, and DatasetDetailSheet already composes exactly this set. This step is a composition of working parts, not new capability — which is why its risk sits almost entirely in T07's navigation and reconciliation, not in its panels.

STALE CORRECTION (2026-08-20): the prior finding here claimed DataAnalysisCard is 'reusable but type-gated' — checked against the code and that is wrong on three counts, not one. (1) It reads dwDraftIdAtom/dwDraftArtifactIdAtom/dwDraftGoldArtifactIdAtom directly (data-studio create wizard's own store) — a dataset-review step in the MODEL wizard has none of those atoms populated. (2) Its histogram/boxplot/scatter tabs call useDatasetHistogram/useDatasetBoxplot/useDatasetScatter, which hit POST .../dataset-drafts/:draftId/artifacts/:artifactId/{histogram,boxplot,scatter} — DRAFT-scoped routes with no saved-dataset (datasetId-scoped) twin; only correlation has one (getArtifactCorrelationService). (3) It renders FeatureTransformDialog (feature-engineering/transformation-panel.tsx) behind a Transform tab and owns dwScalerConfigsAtom — a mutation surface, inside a step whose own contract (finding below) says it configures nothing. The BoundedSample brand gate is real but is not the blocker; the component's data source is. RESOLVED with the user 2026-08-20: T05 does NOT reuse DataAnalysisCard. It composes the review panel from the dataset-scoped hooks the finding above already names (useArtifactRows for a bounded preview + useArtifactCorrelation for top pairs), the same composition DatasetDetailSheet already proves. Acceptance criterion 5 and V02 are rewritten accordingly.

THE STEP HOLDS NO SERVER STATE OF ITS OWN. It reads the dataset's committed artifact and configures nothing. ModelDraft needs no new column and receives no PATCH from this step — stated up front so it is not given one by reflex.

EDITING A DATASET DOES NOT REMOVE IT. The Dataset row keeps its id; what changes is currentArtifactId, and possibly the tag list. So `datasetId` on the ModelDraft stays valid across an edit and must NOT be cleared. What can genuinely go stale is the selected TARGET, if the edit dropped that tag — a different field with a different consequence.

Do this FIRST: a step inserted before its own contract is updated is a step nothing describes. Add one line stating that a dataset selected at Step 1 is reviewable before any training is configured, so the new step has a contract rather than only a position.

tasks.title: Validation-holdout panel
tasks.detail:
CORRECTED SCOPE 2026-08-20: checked against the code and the holdout's missing/Bad rate exists NOWHERE — not on DatasetArtifact, not in ArtifactStatsSchema/ArtifactStats, not computed anywhere in artifact_service.py. The holdout window itself also has no client-facing read path: it lives on the BRONZE sibling of the run's GOLD/FINAL artifact, resolved by runId — the same lookup tryReplayHoldout (model-run.authorized.service.ts) already does server-side, never exposed to a browser. This is a real build, not a composition of existing reads:

1. Python — artifact_service.py's materialize() holdout branch and resplit_holdout() both already hold validate_frame in memory; pass missing_pct(validate_frame) (object_store.py) into _stats_payload as a new validation_missing_pct field. ArtifactStatsResponse (schemas/preprocess.py) gains the field, nullable/optional like validation_row_count beside it.
2. Prisma — DatasetArtifact.validationMissingPct Float?, migrated.
3. Backend — ArtifactStatsSchema (dataset-version.authorized.dto.ts) gains validation_missing_pct; persisted in both places that already set validationRowCount (dataset-version.authorized.service.ts and dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts).
4. New read endpoint GET /datasets/:id/artifacts/:artifactId/holdout: resolve the artifact's runId, find its BRONZE sibling, and if validationRowCount is set return {holdoutFrom, holdoutTo, rowCount, missingPct} — window bounds from Python /metadata against validateDataKey (footer-only, bounded), missingPct from the new column.

THE MISSING RATE IS NOT OPTIONAL for any holdout captured going forward. A holdout written before this change returns missingPct: null, and the panel says so plainly ('missing rate not recorded for this holdout') rather than omitting the field silently or inventing a compute-on-read scan (which would defeat the bounded-read discipline V03 checks). DS-LAKE-018's resolved no-imputation decision means the holdout stays raw, so a MISSING_VALUE hole reaches predict() and depresses the score with no trace of why; its own T05 already requires the rate be published beside every metric for that reason.

tasks.title: Edit Dataset hand-off — warn, persist, reconcile
tasks.detail:
DEFERRED 2026-08-20: out of scope for the T01-T06 pass (composition of the review step itself). Explicitly NOT started because its own dialog-copy rule below is coupled to T08 shipping, and T08 has not. When picked up: PATCH the draft to current BEFORE navigating. useModelDraftSync's PATCH is 600ms-debounced, so a click landing inside that window leaves the server row stale; ensureDraftId already exists for this class of 'the server must know before we do something irreversible' problem.

DO NOT clear datasetId — see findings. Clearing it would discard a reference that stayed valid and force the user to re-pick something that never changed.

RECONCILE ON RETURN, by whatever path: re-fetch the dataset, invalidate every artifact-keyed hook, and CHECK THE TARGET STILL EXISTS in the new artifact's tag list. A dropped target surviving in mpTargetVariableAtom fails at run creation with a pyarrow 'No match for FieldRef.Name' error that names a column and explains nothing — the same class of failure the Step 3.1 correlation tab already hit once.

DIALOG COPY MUST MATCH WHAT SHIPS: it may claim the draft is saved and resumable only if T08 ships. If T08 is cut, the copy says the configuration is discarded. A dialog promising a resume nothing can honour is worse than one admitting the loss.

tasks.title: Resume an ACTIVE ModelDraft from the models list
tasks.detail: DEFERRED 2026-08-20, out of scope for the T01-T06 pass. CORRECTED CLAIM: the prior detail here said 'the draft row already holds every field the wizard would restore' — checked against packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma's ModelDraft model and that is false. It has name/workspaceId/plantId/nodeId/datasetId/targetY/algorithm/hyperparameters/splitRatio/status/currentRunId — no description, no algorithms[] (multi-algorithm selection), no lossFunction, no selectedMetrics, no deploy config (autoRetrain/warnSd/criticalSd/driftMonitor/driftThresholdPct). Restore from this row is PARTIAL. The controller (model-draft.authorized.controller.ts) also has no list route yet — only POST, GET /:id, PATCH /:id, POST /:id/abandon; a GET /model-drafts?workspaceId=&status=ACTIVE is needed first. The step-position part of this task is still fine as originally scoped (derivable from status + currentRunId, no schema change) — only the 'every field' claim was wrong. When picked up, the resume dialog/toast must say what actually restores, not imply full parity.

acceptance_criteria: The wizard has five steps, and this file's own definition of done says five rather than still claiming four.
No existing step's behaviour changes — only its number.
The review step reads the dataset's committed artifact and configures nothing; ModelDraft gains no column and receives no PATCH from it.
Per-tag statistics are served from the sidecar without opening data.parquet.

The review step's preview comes from a bounded server page (useArtifactRows: 200 rows x 50 tags) and top-correlated pairs from useArtifactCorrelation; the step reads no dw* atom and mounts no dataset-wizard mutation UI (revised 2026-08-20 — see the finding on DataAnalysisCard's actual data source).
A dataset with no committed artifact shows one honest empty state, not four independent ones.
The holdout panel publishes the holdout's missing/Bad rate beside every figure it shows.
Leaving to edit a dataset persists the draft first, and the dialog states exactly what survives.
Returning after an edit re-reads the dataset and clears a target the edit removed, saying so.
An ACTIVE ModelDraft is reachable from the models list.

verification.description: Walk the five-step wizard end to end and confirm each pre-existing step behaves exactly as before its renumbering — T01's contract rewrite tested rather than asserted.

REVISED 2026-08-20 (T05 no longer uses DataAnalysisCard — see the finding above): prove the review step's preview goes through useArtifactRows with its bounded params (not an unbounded fetch), and that the step's source file imports no dw* atom from store/dataset-studio and no DataAnalysisCard.

Open the step for a dataset with 8,000 tags and confirm every payload stays bounded — metadata from the footer, statistics from the sidecar, rows from a bounded page. DS-LAKE-012 found a real unbounded /rows fetch at exactly this width (76MB -> 489KB after the fix); a new consumer of the same hooks is where that regression reappears.

PROVE RECONCILIATION, NOT JUST NAVIGATION: leave to edit, DELETE THE SELECTED TARGET TAG, save, return — and confirm the target is cleared and stated. Returning with an intact dataset would pass a weaker test while leaving the failure this task exists to prevent completely uncovered.
Leave to edit, then reach the draft again from the models list and confirm Step 1's choices are restored — the claim T07's dialog makes, verified end to end rather than at the row level.

features.title: ModelDraft Lifecycle Reclaim
features.description: DS-LAKE-014 gave DatasetDraft a sweeper and closed the never-abandoned-ACTIVE hole for datasets. ModelDraft is a separate table with no equivalent, so the identical leak exists here: a user who closes the tab leaves an ACTIVE ModelDraft forever, because nothing calls /abandon on their behalf.
findings: DELIBERATELY NOT A TASK INSIDE MODEL-FLOW-002. That feature is completed at 100% with nine live-verified tasks; reopening it to add reclaim work would make its own completion claim false and mix verified history with unstarted work. The concerns are also independent — 002 gives the container a row to read, this decides when an unused row is released, and neither constrains the other. The DS-LAKE side already answered this question the same way: the DatasetDraft entity is DS-LAKE-005 and its sweeper is DS-LAKE-014, nine features apart.

THE STORAGE COST IS SMALLER THAN THE DATASET CASE BUT NOT ZERO. A ModelDraft owns no artifact of its own, so an abandoned one leaks a Postgres row rather than object bytes. Its ModelTrainingRuns DO write under drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/ (MODEL-FLOW-003-T08), and nothing reclaims those today — so the leak is real, just concentrated in the runs rather than the draft.

MODEL-FLOW-010-T07 MAKES THIS MORE FREQUENT, NOT MERELY MORE VISIBLE. Leaving the wizard to edit a dataset becomes a normal, encouraged action there; every user who does not come back leaves an ACTIVE draft behind. The leak predates that feature but its rate does not.

tasks.title: Tiered ACTIVE-draft eligibility for ModelDraft
tasks.detail: Mirror DS-LAKE-014's tiers rather than inventing a second policy: a draft owning ZERO runs releases on a short window (nothing was computed, nothing is expensive to lose); a draft owning runs releases on a long idle window (a real fit cost minutes of container time). Measure from updatedAt, the same convention DS-LAKE-014's branches use and the same one DS-LAKE-009B-T08 already had to fix once by moving OFF artifact.createdAt. A TRAINED draft is NOT eligible on either window — it holds a finished result the user may still be reviewing in Step 4, which is exactly the state Save Model consumes.

tasks.title: Reclaim the runs' object prefixes, not only the rows
tasks.detail: Abandoning a draft must also release drafts/{modelDraftId}/runs/{runId}/ for each of its runs — otherwise the row disappears and its bytes stay, which is the worse half of the leak and the half nothing currently addresses. is_draft_run_key (MODEL-FLOW-000-T09, MODEL-FLOW-003-T08) is the structural guard that makes a prefix delete safe here; use it rather than a string prefix match.

tasks.title: Periodic sweep caller
tasks.detail: setInterval(...).unref() in onModuleInit, matching DS-LAKE-014's chosen mechanism and PreprocessingJobService.scheduleStragglerSweep's existing precedent — not @nestjs/schedule, which would introduce a second scheduling idiom for one interval. Env-configurable with <= 0 disabling it. Errors logged and swallowed: a failed sweep must never crash the app, and anything it would have reclaimed stays eligible for the next tick.

tasks.title: Reconcile orphaned RUNNING runs at boot
tasks.detail: Found during MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's live verification, not in the original scope: run 562ec955 sat at RUNNING with zero log lines after a nest --watch restart killed watch()'s in-memory tracker mid-flight. The container is independent of the Node process, so nothing reconciles a run whose watcher died. That row is now permanently RUNNING — never terminal, so never eligible under any window this feature adds. Reconcile at boot: for each RUNNING run, check whether its container still exists and mark it FAILED with a stated reason if not.

acceptance_criteria: An ACTIVE ModelDraft with no runs becomes eligible after the short window and is reclaimed with no operator action.
An ACTIVE ModelDraft owning runs is not reclaimed on the short window.
A TRAINED draft is never reclaimed by either window.
Reclaiming a draft also releases its runs' object prefixes.
A RUNNING run whose container no longer exists reaches a terminal status at boot rather than staying RUNNING forever.
The sweep runs without any HTTP call, and disabling it via env leaves any admin path working unchanged.

verification.description: Seed an ACTIVE ModelDraft with zero runs past the short window; run the sweep against real Postgres and confirm it is reclaimed.

PROVE THE TIER BITES BOTH WAYS: a draft WITH runs, past the short window but inside the long one, must survive the same sweep run that reclaims V01's draft. One run, two drafts, opposite outcomes — a test that only proves reclamation cannot distinguish a working tier from a blanket rule.
Confirm a reclaimed draft's run prefixes are actually gone from MinIO, asserting a non-zero delete count. A prefix bug reports success having deleted nothing.
Reproduce the V01-observed orphan: start a run, kill the backend mid-flight, restart, and confirm the RUNNING row reaches a terminal status.

global_definition_of_done: The five-step Model Creation Flow is preserved.
A dataset selected at Step 1 is reviewable at Step 2 before any training is configured.
Step 3 Training Configuration behavior remains unchanged.
Step 5 Save Model behavior remains unchanged...
Training runs without committing the Model to the database.
Evaluation works without a persistent Model database record.
Fine-Tuning runs as a background process.
Fine-Tuning does not commit the Model to the database.
Model configuration is preserved before final Save Model.
Model artifacts are stored and referenced correctly.
Save Model is the only persistence boundary for the final Model.
Failed Save Model operations do not leave partial Model records.
No unrelated functionality is changed or broken.
No persistent MODEL record is created before Save Model. Draft, job and log rows ARE written before it — they are what makes a container able to run and report at all.
Every metric shown in Step 3 comes from a run whose target-leakage guard actually executed.
